arxiv-2107-02330.title: Measurement of emission spectrum for gaseous argon electroluminescence in visible light region from 300 to 600 nm Journal: Nucl. Instrum. Methods. Phys. Res. A
arxiv-2107-02330.creator: Kazutaka Aoyama, Masato Kimura, Hiroyuki Morohoshi, Tomomasa Takeda, Masashi Tanaka, Kohei Yorita
arxiv-2107-02330.description: Abstract A double-phase Ar detector can efficiently identify particles and reconstruct their positions. However, the properties of electroluminescence (EL) for secondary light emission in the gas phase are not fully understood. Earlier studies have explained the EL process using an ordinary EL mechanism because of an Ar excimer; however, this mechanism does not predict the emission of visible light (VL).

arxiv-2112-06426.title: Anticharmed strange pentaquarks from the one-boson-exchange model
arxiv-2112-06426.creator: Nijiati Yalikun, Bing-Song Zou
arxiv-2112-06426.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Nijiati Yalikun, Bing-Song Zou. Inspired by the LHCb’s discovery of hidden-charm pentaquarks, the anticharmed strange pentaquarks P c ¯ ​ s P_{\bar{c}s} in a favor of the hadronic molecule picture are investigated from the one-boson-exchange model.

arxiv-2210-05039.title: Contrastive Video-Language Learning with Fine-grained Frame Sampling
arxiv-2210-05039.creator: Zixu Wang, Yujie Zhong, Yishu Miao, Lin Ma, Lucia Specia
arxiv-2210-05039.description: Abstract Despite recent progress in video and language representation learning, the weak or sparse correspondence between the two modalities remains a bottleneck in the area. Most video-language models are trained via pair-level loss to predict whether a pair of video and text is aligned.

arxiv-2301-13754.title: CMB signature of non-thermal Dark Matter produced from self-interacting dark sector
arxiv-2301-13754.creator: Dilip Kumar Ghosh, Purusottam Ghosh, Sk Jeesun
arxiv-2301-13754.description: Abstract The basic idea of this work is to achieve the observed relic density of a non-thermal dark matter(DM) and its connection with Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) via additional relativistic degrees of freedom which are simultaneously generated during the period T BBN ​ to ​ T CMB T_{\rm BBN}~{\rm to}~T_{\rm CMB} from a long-lived dark sector particle.

arxiv-2401-05044.title: Universal hard-edge statistics of non-Hermitian random matrices
arxiv-2401-05044.creator: Zhenyu Xiao, Ryuichi Shindou, Kohei Kawabata
arxiv-2401-05044.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zhenyu Xiao, Ryuichi Shindou, Kohei Kawabata. Random matrix theory is a powerful tool for understanding spectral correlations inherent in quantum chaotic systems. Despite diverse applications of non-Hermitian random matrix theory, the role of symmetry remains to be fully established. Here, we comprehensively investigate the impact of symmetry on the level statistics around the spectral origin—hard-edge statistics—and expand the classification of spectral statistics to encompass all the 38 symmetry classes of non-Hermitian random matrices.

arxiv-2402-05195.title: λ \lambda -ECLIPSE : Multi-Concept Personalized Text-to-Image Diffusion Models by Leveraging CLIP Latent Space
arxiv-2402-05195.creator: Maitreya Patel, Sangmin JungChitta BaralYezhou YangArizona State University https://eclipse-t2i.github.io/Lambda-ECLIPSE/
arxiv-2402-05195.description: Abstract Despite the recent advances in personalized text-to-image (P-T2I) generative models, it remains challenging to perform finetuning-free multi-subject-driven T2I in a resource-efficient manner. Predominantly, contemporary approaches, involving the training of Hypernetworks and Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), require heavy computing resources that range from 600 to 12300 GPU hours of training.

arxiv-2403-03237.title: Local Quantum Search Algorithm for Random k k -SAT with Ω ⁡ ( n 1 + ϵ ) \Omega(n^{1+\epsilon}) Clauses
arxiv-2403-03237.creator: Mingyou Wu
arxiv-2403-03237.description: Abstract The random k k -SAT instances undergo a “phase transition” from being generally satisfiable to unsatisfiable as the clause number m m passes a critical threshold, r k ​ n r_{k}n . This causes a drastic reduction in the number of satisfying assignments, shifting the problem from being generally solvable on classical computers to typically insolvable.

arxiv-2404-18432.title: Structure-preserving particle methods for the Landau collision operator using the metriplectic framework
arxiv-2404-18432.creator: S. Jeyakumar, M. Kraus, M. J. Hole, D. Pfefferlé
arxiv-2404-18432.description: Abstract We present a novel family of particle discretisation methods for the nonlinear Landau collision operator. We exploit the metriplectic structure underlying the Vlasov–Maxwell–Landau system in order to obtain disretisation schemes that automatically preserve mass, momentum, and energy, warrant monotonic dissipation of entropy, and are thus guaranteed to respect the laws of thermodynamics.

arxiv-2406-15626.title: Deducibility in the full Lambek calculus with weakening is HAck -complete
arxiv-2406-15626.creator: Vitor Greati, Revantha Ramanayake
arxiv-2406-15626.description: Abstract We show that the problem of deciding the consequence relation (deducibility) for the full Lambek calculus with weakening ( 𝐅𝐋 𝐰 \mathbf{FL}_{\mathbf{w}} ) is complete for the class HAck of hyper-Ackermannian problems (i.e., 𝐅 ω ω \mathbf{F}_{\omega^{\omega}} in the ordinal-indexed hierarchy of fast-growing complexity classes). Provability was already known to be PSpace -complete.

arxiv-2503-11785.title: Near-Term Fermionic Simulation with Subspace Noise Tailored Quantum Error Mitigation
arxiv-2503-11785.creator: Miha Papič, Manuel G. Algaba, Emiliano Godinez-Ramirez, Inés de Vega, Adrian Auer, Fedor Šimkovic IV, Alessio Calzona
arxiv-2503-11785.description: Abstract Quantum error mitigation (QEM) has emerged as a powerful tool for the extraction of useful quantum information from quantum devices. Here, we introduce the Subspace Noise Tailoring (SNT) algorithm, which efficiently combines the cheap cost of Symmetry Verification (SV) and low bias of Probabilistic Error Cancellation (PEC) QEM techniques.

arxiv-2509-14186.title: Quickest Change Detection with Cost-Constrained Experiment Design
arxiv-2509-14186.creator: Patrick Vincent N. Lubenia, Taposh Banerjee
arxiv-2509-14186.description: Abstract In the classic quickest change detection problem, an observer performs only one experiment to monitor a stochastic process. This paper considers the case where, at each observation time, the decision-maker needs to choose between multiple experiments with different information qualities and costs. The goal is to minimize the worst-case average detection delay subject to false alarm and cost constraints.

arxiv-2602-15112.title: ResearchGym: Evaluating Language Model Agents on Real-World AI Research
arxiv-2602-15112.creator: Aniketh Garikaparthi, Manasi Patwardhan, Arman Cohan, [8pt] TCS Research
arxiv-2602-15112.description: Abstract We introduce ResearchGym, a benchmark and execution environment for evaluating AI agents on end-to-end research. To instantiate this, we repurpose five oral and spotlight papers from ICML, ICLR, and ACL. From each paper’s repository, we preserve the datasets, evaluation harness, and baseline implementations but withhold the paper’s proposed method.

arxiv-2606-23548.creator: Nandana Menon, Giorgio Vallone

pmc-11320772.title: Assessment of impaired glomerular filtration rate and associated factors in South West Ethiopia: a cross-sectional study
pmc-11320772.creator: Bisrat Fikadu Habtu, Gizachew Ayele, Habtamu Belay, Seid Abrar, Dereje Abebe, Nigus Chekole
pmc-11320772.description: IntroductionCurrently, kidney disease is an increasing major health problem worldwide. It is expected to be the 5th ranked cause of death by 2040. If it is early detected, further complication caused by kidney disease will be minimized. An assessment of impaired glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) has potential aids in early identification and treatment of kidney disease.

pmc-12608716.title: X-Linked Hypophosphatemia in a Family Cohort: Clinical Variability, Genetic Confirmation and Modern Therapeutic Perspectives
pmc-12608716.creator: Oana Popa, Melania Balaș, Ioana Golu, Daniela Amzăr, Carmen Dorogi, Mihaela Vlad, Fernando Cordido
pmc-12608716.description: Background/Objectives: X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) is the most common form of inherited rickets, caused by pathogenic mutations in the PHEX gene (phosphate-regulating endopeptidase homolog, X-linked). These mutations increase fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) activity, resulting in renal phosphate wasting and defective bone mineralization. The disorder manifests with variable skeletal, dental, and extraskeletal involvement.

pmc-12651592.title: Genomic and Demographic Characteristics of Angiosarcoma as Described in the AACR Project GENIE Registry
pmc-12651592.creator: Eileen Leach, Amir Jafari, Elijah Torbenson, Beau Hsia, Abubakar Tauseef, Tarek Abbas
pmc-12651592.description: Simple SummaryIn this study, we analyzed the AACR GENIE registry to characterize genomic and demographic characteristics of angiosarcoma. Angiosarcoma carries high mortality but has low prevalence, and consequently, there are limited large-scale genomic studies. Though prior studies have identified mutations associated with angiosarcoma, this is the first study to specifically analyze angiosarcoma genomics in the AACR GENIE database.

pmc-13046771.title: Acyl-CoA-binding protein (ACBP): a poor-prognosis biomarker in sepsis and a target for disease mitigation
pmc-13046771.creator: Flavia Lambertucci, Omar Motiño, Uxía Nogueira-Recalde, Yan Rong, Léa Montégut, María Pérez-Lanzón, Vincent Carbonnier, Sijing Li, Sylvère Durand, Fanny Aprahamian, Hui Chen, Yanbing Dong, Allan Sauvat, Silvia Mingoia, Sylvie Lachkar, Ester Saavedra, Jonathan Pol, Federico Pietrocola, Maria Chiara M
pmc-13046771.description: Sepsis remains a major clinical challenge, with high mortality and long-term disability despite current interventions. Here, we identify the tissue hormone acyl-CoA-binding protein (ACBP), also known as diazepam-binding inhibitor (DBI), as a biomarker and driver of poor outcome in sepsis. ACBP/DBI was elevated in the plasma of septic patients and associated with organ dysfunction and increased mortality.

pmc-13219232.title: Measuring capacities to advance global health security and bioeconomic development on the African continent
pmc-13219232.creator: Margaret M Dunne, Yenew Kebede, Wilmot James, Ali Asy, Peter Ahabwe Babigumira, Donewell Bangure, Ian Peter Busuulwa, Rym Benkhalifa, Joseph Bitilinyu-Bangoh, Elizabeth E Cameron, Carly Gasca, Christopher R Isaac, Issa Makumbi, Talkmore Maruta, Zibusiso Masuku, Natalie Mayet, Diane Meyer, Geoffrey N
pmc-13219232.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights•Health security capacities are crucial to reduce the risks from infectious diseases.•African countries demonstrate a strong commitment to improving health security.•The biosafety and biosecurity capacities of African countries need strengthening.•Enhancing health security boosts preparedness and supports Africa’s bioeconomy.Keywords: Global health, Health security, Infectious diseases, One Health, Epidemiology

Background

The African continent continues to face a disproportionately high burden of infectious disease outbreaks [1].

pmc-13328433.title: Neuromorphic-inspired multi-view global-local fusion for IR-UWB radar dynamic gesture recognition
pmc-13328433.creator: Guoyi Xue, Junhong Yang, Hui Zhu

pmc-13478640.title: Behavior-aware deep reinforcement learning for multi-objective outpatient scheduling optimization
pmc-13478640.creator: Xiaoyu Wan, Xiayan Zhang, Weiqun Weng, Pu Han, Xiangyun Xu
pmc-13478640.description: Outpatient departments in large hospitals face persistent scheduling inefficiencies characterized by prolonged patient waiting, underutilized resources, and high no-show rates. Existing scheduling approaches largely ignore the behavioral heterogeneity of patients, treating satisfaction as a simple proxy of waiting time rather than a psychologically grounded construct.

pmc-13586224.title: Cardiopulmonary hospitalization risks from wildfire-specific and non-wildfire PM2.5 in 20 US states
pmc-13586224.creator: Min Zhang, Edgar Castro, Minghao Qiu, Mahdieh Danesh Yazdi, Boyuan Li, Rosalind J Wright, Joel D Schwartz, Robert O Wright, Yaguang Wei
pmc-13586224.description: Increasing wildfire activity in the US has made wildfire-specific fine particulate matter (PM2.5) an important and growing source of air pollution, yet its long-term health impacts and relative toxicity compared with non-wildfire PM2.5 remain unclear. Using a self-controlled design, we examine associations between 2-year average wildfire-specific and non-wildfire PM2.5 and cardiopulmonary hospitalization risks across 20 US states during 2006–2019.

pmc-13672886.title: The role of glymphatic dysfunction in cerebral small vessel disease and vascular cognitive impairment, and therapeutic implications
pmc-13672886.creator: Hui Hong, Yutong Chen, Peiyu Huang, Hugh S Markus
pmc-13672886.description: Background:The glymphatic system is a brain-wide perivascular clearance pathway that facilitates cerebrospinal fluid–interstitial fluid (CSF-ISF) exchange and the removal of metabolic waste from the brain parenchyma. Increasing evidence indicates that glymphatic transport is critically dependent on the integrity and function of cerebral small vessels, suggesting a close link with cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD).
